h: Kindness Fear and Humility Within the Priestly Blessing

p: In the holy Zohar on this parshah
כָּל מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם
is called an angel of Hashem of Hosts;
'For the lips of the Kohen guard knowledge,
and they seek Torah from his mouth,
for he is an angel of Hashem of Hosts,'" etc.
"And because the Kohen is called a chassid,
'And Your pious ones will bless You'
are found in Aharon the Kohen:
"I gave them to him for fear, and he feared Me," etc.;
"Your Tumim and Your Urim to Your pious one";
the aspect of the holiness of the holy Avos:
are the aspects of Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov,
as we have spoken many times.
which go forth from the mouth of a Kohen
of the three traits mentioned above
certainly there is alluded in the blessings too
the perfection of the three traits mentioned above.
and Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
to feed all who came into the world
"And he called there in the Name of Hashem," etc.,
that he taught them the way of Hashem
as our Sages, of blessed memory, said in the Midrash.
And likewise what is written in Sukkah (49b):
"One might think anyone who wishes may leap forward, etc.;
That is, kindness for the body
its essence is when one does through it
like Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him;
and this is called "Your kindness, O God,"
דְּזֶהוּ חֶסֶד ה׳ וְגוֹ׳ עַל יְרֵאָיו
for this is "the kindness of Hashem," etc., "upon those who fear Him" (Tehillim 103:17),
כִּי מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם
for one who has fear of Heaven,
and through this he merits piety,
who "brings them close to the Torah,"
for his words enter the heart of the listener.
which is the matter of increase in the flow,
הוּא עַל הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
is on the innovation of the Oral Torah.
after Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
that halachos that had been forgotten
and for this he was called Yaavetz,
for he counseled and spread Torah, etc.
And it is called "a Torah of kindness,"
which is not so with the Written Torah,
where there is a limit and a number
and we are warned against adding.
וְכֵן מָצִינוּ בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And so we find with Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, provided him
And the main flow of kindness
alludes to teaching Torah to others,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוּכָּה מט, ב)
as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sukkah 49b):
this is a Torah of kindness."
"The poor man and the man of means meet,"
about a student with his teacher:
about a poor man and a rich man
for in the flow of Torah
and also from teaching a student who is unworthy,
"May Hashem shine His face upon you"
alludes to the aspect of fear,
the revelation of the light of His face, may He be blessed,
as our Sages, of blessed memory, said
this is the revelation of the Shechinah."
for the matter of finding favor
is found in the aspect of fear,
as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Shabbos 31b):
לֹא בָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹלָמוֹ
"The Holy One, blessed be He, created His world
only so that they should fear Him,
And our Sages, of blessed memory, said in Midrash Rabbah
that the Holy One, blessed be He, said:
if only you would find favor before Me
"May Hashem lift His face toward you"
corresponds to the aspect of humility,
as our Sages, of blessed memory, said
"'Who bears iniquity for the remnant of His heritage' (Michah 7:18)
for one who makes himself like leftovers,"
And so our Sages, of blessed memory, said
that the Holy One, blessed be He, said:
"How shall I not show them favor,
when they are exacting with themselves
to the size of an olive and of an egg?"
praise and thanks to Hashem, may He be blessed,
for what He bestowed upon them,
even the scant olive's and egg's measure,
because they are not worthy in their own eyes
out of the aspect of humility
for after one is completed in the perfection
of the rectification of the three traits mentioned above,
from all the battles and accusations
that this is the reason for the juxtaposition of all the parshiyos:
the sending out of the impure:
the metzora, the zav, and one impure through the dead,
which is the rectification of the three general blemishes,
as we have spoken of this many times.
After this is stated the mitzvah of teshuvah,
which is the culmination of the rectification.
After this is the parshah of the sotah,
שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן עִנְיַן בֵּירוּר הַנֶּפֶשׁ
which is also a matter of refining the soul;
as is known, the meal offering of jealousy
is alluded to in the counting of the barley Omer,
to purify us from our impurities.
are alluded to in the waters of Marah,
and as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Yoma 72b):
זָכָה נַעֲשֵׂית לוֹ סַם חַיִּים וְכוּלֵּי
"If he merits, it becomes for him an elixir of life," etc.
After this is stated the parshah of the nazir,
from the three blemishes mentioned above,
alluded to in the prohibitions of impurity,
of shaving, and of what comes from the vine:
as we have said many times;
and what comes from the vine
as is written, "much wine causes" it;
and shaving corresponds to the aspect of anger,
as is known, that the Levi'im,
who are from the side of judgment
while the nazir is the opposite,
because he is called "a nazir of God,"
After this is stated Birkas Kohanim,
which is the perfection of the three traits,
"And it was on the day Moshe finished,"
which is the perfection of the union,
of the bride's entry into the bridal canopy.

— “On the day that Moses finished setting up the Tabernacle, he anointed and consecrated it and all its furnishings, as well as the altar and its utensils. When he had anointed and consecrated them,”
